Nature of the Case : Seeking  Compensation/Award  SCCH-8 3 MVC No.2437/2022 Date of commencement of : 06.01.2023 Recording of evidence Date of Judgment : 09.07.2025 pronounced  JUDGMENT Yashodamma vs Rajanna .B.H on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82601040/

The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming the compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- from the respondents with regard to the death of Hanumanthaiah, in the road traffic accident that took place on 23.04.2022.
2.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioners as follows:
On 23.04.2022 at about 3.19 p.m., when deceased Hanumanthaiah was riding his Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA- 36-EA-6997 near Falukere Temple Sirivara-Hebburu Road, Kembalalu Station, Tumkuru District, at that time, driver of the Tractor and Trailer bearing Reg. Nos.KA-06-TD-7668 and KA-06- TD-7669 came in a rash and negligent manner and suddenly put a break and without giving any indication stopped the vehicle in the middle of the road, due to which deceased dashed against the Tractor and Trailer.
On account of the tremendous impact of the said accident, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

It is contended that, immediately after the accident, injured was shifted to Government hospital, Tumkuru wherein duty doctor was examined deceased and declared as brought dead on the way to hospital.

Thereafter, the post-mortem was conducted and the dead body was handed over to the petitioners and they have performed the last rites and obsequies of the deceased by spending huge amount towards medical and funeral expenses.
3.
It is stated that the deceased was working as Supervisor at JBM Bricks Industries, Gangasandra and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
The deceased was the only bread earner of their family and due to his death, the petitioners are undergoing mental shock and agony and facing great financial difficulties.
It is further stated that the accident in question was due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending Tractor and Trailer bearing Reg. Nos.KA-06-TD-7668 and KA-06-TD-7669.
Hence, the 1st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicles are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
4. On service of notice, both the respondents appeared before the court through their respective counsels and the 2 nd respondent filed written statement.
5. The 2nd Respondent in its objections has stated that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and hence the petition is liable to be dismissed.
It has denied the age, income and occupation of the deceased.
It has also denied the amount spent towards the funeral expenses of the deceased.

This respondent has admitted the issuance Policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of the offending Tractor and Trailer bearing Reg. Nos.KA- 06-TD-7668 and KA-06-TD-7669 and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further stated that, the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license and Permit at the time of the accident.
It is contended that the insured of the offending vehicle has violated Section 134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
It has denied the alleged negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
It is contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners are high exorbitant.
On other grounds pray for dismissal of the petition.

3

6. Based on the pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed following issues:-
ISSUES
1. Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Sri.Hanumanthaiah?

2. Whether the petitioners prove that on 23.04.2022 at about 3.19 p.m., near Falukere Temple, Sririvara- Hebburu road, Kembalalu Palya, Hebburu Hobli, Tumkuru, the driver of the Tractor and Trailer bearing Reg. Nos.KA-06-TD-7668 and KA-06-TD-7669 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased Sri. Hanumanthaiah who was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-36-EA-6997 due to which he sustained injuries and later succumbed due to injuries ?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for any compensation? If so, to what extent and from whom?
4. What order or Award?
7.
In order to prove the case, 1 st petitioner got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to 13 documents.
On the other hand, respondent No.2 has examined two witnesses as RW.1 and RW.2 and got marked Ex.R1 to Ex.R5 documents.

8. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for petitioner and perused the written arguments submitted by the learned counsel for respondent No.2.
9.

My findings on the above issues as under:-
Issue No.1 ... In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 ... In the Affirmative, Issue No.3 ... Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.4 ...

As per final order For the following:
REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.2 : It is the case of the petitioners that, on 23.04.2022 at about 3.19 p.m., when deceased Hanumanthaiah was riding his Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-36-EA-6997 near Falukere Temple Sirivara-Hebburu Road, Kembalalu Station, Tumkuru District, at that time, driver of the Tractor and Trailer bearing Reg. Nos.KA-06-TD-7668 and KA-06-TD-7669 came in a rash and negligent manner and suddenly put a break and without giving any indication stop the vehicle in the middle of the road and deceased was dashed against the Tractor and Trailer, caused the accident, due to which he sustained grievous injuries and later succumbed to the injuries.

It is specifically urged that, the accident happened because of the rash and negligent act of the offending vehicle driver and as such the respondents are liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

Yashodamma vs Rajanna .B.H on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82601040/
4 11.

In order to substantiate the contentions of the petitioners, the petitioner No.1 stepped into the witness box and filed her affidavit-in-lieu of oral examination-in-chief as PW1 and got marked F.I.R,
F.I.S, spot mahazar, Seizure mahazar, IMV report, P.M. Report, Inquest report and charge sheet as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P8.
12.

On the other hand, respondent No.2 has contended that the alleged accident was occurred due to the deceased himself who was riding the two wheeler after consuming alcohol and rode it in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the left side stationed tractor and trailer from back side and FSL Report says that the deceased had consumed quantum of alcohol at 37.28 mg.
At the time of accident and also he was riding two wheeler without DL.

In order to prove the same, respondent No.2 has examined two witnesses as RW.1 who is the Police Inspector, CTSB, Bengaluru and he got marked the documents at Ex.R1 to R4 which are FSL Report, Final expert opinion, 133 notice and reply.

Also examined the Legal Manager of TP Claims of respondent company as RW.2 and he got marked the policy copy at Ex.R5.
13.
This issue revolves round the sphere and ambit as to the alleged rash and negligence on the part of the driver offending vehicle.
The factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence, it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.

These elements are as follows:
Duty: For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Here it is important to understand whether the defendant has taken legal duty of care towards the plaintiff.
Breach of Duty:
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.
Damages: At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.

Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.

Yashodamma vs Rajanna .B.H on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82601040/
5 14.
I have perused documentary evidence coupled with oral evidence in detail.

As per Ex.P1- FIR filed at Cr.No.0097/2022 of Hebbur police station clearly shows that on 23.04.2022 at about 3.00 to 3.10 p.m. there was an accident and in the said accident, deceased was the rider of the motor cycle sustained grievous injuries and and also died on the way to the hospital.

One Sri Narasimharaju has put the law into motion by filing first information and accordingly, Ex.P.1 FIR is registered against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s. 279 and 304(A) of IPC.

Whereas documents at Ex.P-1 to 5 and 8 i.e. FIR, Complaint, Spot panchanama, vehicle seizure mahazar,
IMV report and Charge sheet.

15. It is the contention of the respondent No.2 that the deceased was under the influence of alcohol at the time of accident and also in PM report it is mentioned that the blood in EDTA is sent to FSL for alcohol percentage estimation as requested by investigating officer.

Further on perusal of Ex.R1 FSL Report the director of State Forensic Science Laboratory stated that 37.28 mg out of 100 ml.
blood is containing ethyl alcohol.

16. Further the I.O. also in the charge sheet has mentioned about the said fact of consumption of alcohol as per PM and FSL report and has argued that the accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent act of deceased as he has driven the motor cycle under the influence of alcohol.

The Charge sheet produced by the petitioners clearly discloses that the charge sheet is filed against the driver of the offending vehicle tractor for not giving indicator or signal and for stopping the vehicle in the middle of the road, against the deceased for drink and drive and not holding driving licence at the time of the accident, and also against the owner of the motor cycle for handing over the motor cycle for the person who is not possessing the valid driving licence under section IPC 1860 U/s. 279,
283, 304(A) and under section 180, 181, 185 of M.V. Act.
17.

Whereas the petitioner counsel has argued that even though as per PM and FSL report there is mentioning of consumption of alcohol by the deceased, but the accident has taken place on 23.06.2022 at 3.10 p.m. and PM report is conducted on 24.04.2022 between 11.30 a.m. to 12.30 p.m. for which the PM report and FSL report cannot be considered and further the said consumption of alcohol itself cannot be a ground to hold that the accident has taken place solely due to the rash and negligent act of deceased.

18. I would like to rely upon the decision rendered by Hon'ble Madras High Court in C.Misc.Appeal No.1842/2006 in K.Shanmugam vs. V.Krishnamurthy & Another) wherein it is held that the involvement of claimant in the accident due to the fact that he was in drunken state and also alcohol consumption impairs consciousness and vision which becomes impossible to judge accurately how far the objects are whether it is night or day it can reduce the visibility of an object to the point of being below the limit of discernibility and punishment should be at-least a deterrent for other such persons getting away with minor punishment and fine.
Further, as per section 185 of M.V. Act to be considered as zero tolerance wherein too many lives have already been lost to this lithel coctail of internal consumption and combustion.

The FSL report along with PM report produced by the IO showing 37.28 mg./100 ml. consumption of alcohol is itself is sufficient to come to conclusion that the deceased was under the influence of alcohol at the time of accident and such being the fact, the consumption of the alcohol is to be considered relying upon the said reports as the drink and drive Yashodamma vs Rajanna .B.H on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82601040/
6 has become menace to our society due to which several lives are lost and such act of drink and drive by consuming the alcohol has to be considered seriously and hence considering the charge sheet filed by the I.O. showing the deceased was under the influence of alcohol for which some part of contributory negligence for happening of the accident by the deceased if considered will meet the ends of justice.
19.

Hence, in view of my discussion made earlier it goes to show that, the said accident has taken place on account of negligence of the tractor and trailer driver and also for the rash and negligent act of the rider of motor cycle deceased due to the contributory negligence of both the vehicles.

20. Therefore, in this issue it clearly goes to show that, accident has taken place due to the rash and negligence of both the vehicles attributing to contributory negligence for which the rider of the motor cycle/deceased is saddled @ 20% and driver of the offending tractor and trailer is saddled with 80% contributory negligence for the cause of accident, because the driver tractor and trailer not giving indicator or signal and for stopping the vehicle in the middle of the road and accordingly I answer Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
21. ISSUE No.1 and 3:
While answering issue No.2, I have already observed that accident has taken place due to the rash and negligence of both the vehicles attributing to the contributory negligence.
The petitioners claim that, Petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioners No.2 and 3 are the children and petitioner No.4 is the mother of the deceased.
To prove the same, petitioner No.1 filed affidavit in lieu of her chief-examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The Aadhar cards marked at Ex's.P.9 to 13 and contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.
It is pertinent to note that, the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased has not been disputed by the respondents.

Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners are the legal representative of the deceased Hanumanthaiah.

Therefore, petitioners are the legal heir and dependents of deceased and they are entitled for compensation.
22.

The petitioners have contended that the deceased was an Supervisor and earning Rs.30,000/-
per month.
In order to prove the same, petitioners have not produced any documents before the court.
The accident occurred in the year 2022.
Therefore, considering the occupation of the deceased and year of the accident, I deem it just and reasonable to take the notional income of the deceased at Rs.15,500/- per month.
23. It is stated that the deceased was aged 53 years at the time of the accident.
The petitioners have produced Ex.P10 Adhaar card of the deceased which reveals the birth year of the deceased as 1969.
The accident occurred on 23.04.2022.
Hence, the age of the deceased at the time of accident was 53 years.

Hence the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is '11'.
24.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income Yashodamma vs Rajanna .B.H on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82601040/
7 with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years 10%.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 53 years.
Therefore, in this case, 10% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

Hence, 10% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.17,050/-p.m. (Rs.15,500/- +
1,550/- i.e.10%).
The deceased died leaving behind four dependents.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma Case, 1/4th of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses which comes to Rs.12,788/- p.m.(Rs.17,050 - Rs.4,262/-).
25.
The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.12,788/- p.m. and the multiplier '11' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.16,88,016/-(Rs.12,788 X 12 X 11).

Considering the above facts,
this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.16,88,016/- under the head of loss of dependency.

26. Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The PW.1 contended that they have spent substantial amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies etc., but no documents are produced.
Hence this Tribunal award Rs.16,500/- towards loss to estate and Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years.
27. In this case, the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 and 3 are the children and petitioner No.4 is the mother of the deceased.

As per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioners are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of children/father/mother as the case may be.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of a husband, father and son causes great shock and agony to the wife, children and mother of the deceased and they lost their love and affection towards their husband, father and son.
Therefore, petitioners No.1 to 4 are entitled for Rs.44,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.

28. In total, the petitioners are entitled for the compensation under the following heads:
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1.
Towards loss of dependency Rs.16,88,016/-

2. Towards loss of Consortium to the Rs.1,76,000/-

8 3.

Towards loss to estate Rs.16,500/-
4. Towards transportation of dead Rs.16,500/-
 body funeral and obsequies ceremony  expenses  Total Rs.18,97,016/-
 Less: 20% Contributory Negligence of Rs.3,79,403/-
 deceased

Compensation to be payable by the Rs.15,17,613/-
 respondent No.2

In all, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.15,17,613/-.
29.

As regard the apportionment of compensation is concerned, it is not in dispute that the 1 st petitioner is the widow, petitioners No.2 and 3 are the daughter and son and petitioner No.4 is the mother of the deceased.

Hence out of the total compensation, the petitioners No. 1 to 4 are entitled for compensation at the ratio of 50:15:15:20.
30.
The petitioners are claiming interest on the compensation amount.
The respondent No.1 has denied the same.

Our Hon'ble High Court in the case rendered in Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another (MFA.No.100090/2014 C/W MFA.No.25107/2013 dated 07.03.2018), has held that in the absence of any other law relating to interest on judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Sec.34 of C.P.C and awarded interest @ 6% per annum.

sentences.text: Considering the aforesaid decision, I deem it proper to award interest at 6% per annum on the above compensation amount.
31. Liability:

Regarding fixation of liability is concerned, I have already observed that the accident was taken place due to the negligence on the part of the driver of offending Tractor and Trailer bearing Reg. Nos.KA-06-TD-7668 and KA-06-TD-7669.
It is not in dispute that 1st respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
The respondents have not proved the breach of any of the policy conditions.

As already discussed deceased/rider of motor cycle and the driver of tractor and trailer bearing Reg. Nos.KA-06-TD- 7668 and KA-06-TD-7669 have contributed for happening of accident towards contributory negligence @ 20%:80%.
Hence, 1 st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation of its liability of 80%.
The 2 nd respondent shall indemnify the 1st respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative and Issue No.3 Partly in the Affirmative.
32. Issue No.4:
In view of my findings on issues No.1 to 3, I pass the following:
ORDER The petition is allowed in part with cost.

Nos.KA-06-TD-7668 and KA-06-TD-7669 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased Sri. Hanumanthaiah who was riding the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-36-EA-6997 due to which he sustained injuries and later succumbed due to injuries ?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for any compensation? If so, to what extent and from whom?
4. What order or Award?
7.
As per final order For the following:
REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.2 : It is the case of the petitioners that, on 23.04.2022 at about 3.19 p.m., when deceased Hanumanthaiah was riding his Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-36-EA-6997 near Falukere Temple Sirivara-Hebburu Road, Kembalalu Station, Tumkuru District, at that time, driver of the Tractor and Trailer bearing Reg. Nos.KA-06-TD-7668 and KA-06-TD-7669 came in a rash and negligent manner and suddenly put a break and without giving any indication stop the vehicle in the middle of the road and deceased was dashed against the Tractor and Trailer, caused the accident, due to which he sustained grievous injuries and later succumbed to the injuries.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The factum of negligence has to be proved like any other fact in issue.
Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence, it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.
These elements are as follows:
Duty: For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Breach of Duty:
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.
Damages: At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.
Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.
The Charge sheet produced by the petitioners clearly discloses that the charge sheet is filed against the driver of the offending vehicle tractor for not giving indicator or signal and for stopping the vehicle in the middle of the road, against the deceased for drink and drive and not holding driving licence at the time of the accident, and also against the owner of the motor cycle for handing over the motor cycle for the person who is not possessing the valid driving licence under section IPC 1860 U/s. 279,
283, 304(A) and under section 180, 181, 185 of M.V. Act.
17.
The FSL report along with PM report produced by the IO showing 37.28 mg./100 ml. consumption of alcohol is itself is sufficient to come to conclusion that the deceased was under the influence of alcohol at the time of accident and such being the fact, the consumption of the alcohol is to be considered relying upon the said reports as the drink and drive Yashodamma vs Rajanna .B.H on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82601040/
6 has become menace to our society due to which several lives are lost and such act of drink and drive by consuming the alcohol has to be considered seriously and hence considering the charge sheet filed by the I.O. showing the deceased was under the influence of alcohol for which some part of contributory negligence for happening of the accident by the deceased if considered will meet the ends of justice.
19.
Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners are the legal representative of the deceased Hanumanthaiah.
Therefore, petitioners are the legal heir and dependents of deceased and they are entitled for compensation.
22.
26. Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.
As per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioners are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of children/father/mother as the case may be.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Considering the above facts,
this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.16,88,016/- under the head of loss of dependency.
Therefore, petitioners No.1 to 4 are entitled for Rs.44,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.
28. In total, the petitioners are entitled for the compensation under the following heads:
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1.
Towards loss of dependency Rs.16,88,016/-
Towards loss to estate Rs.16,500/-
4. Towards transportation of dead Rs.16,500/-
 body funeral and obsequies ceremony  expenses  Total Rs.18,97,016/-
 Less: 20% Contributory Negligence of Rs.3,79,403/-
 deceased
Compensation to be payable by the Rs.15,17,613/-
 respondent No.2
In all, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.15,17,613/-.
29.
Considering the aforesaid decision, I deem it proper to award interest at 6% per annum on the above compensation amount.
Hence, 1 st respondent being the owner and 2nd respondent being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation of its liability of 80%.
The 2 nd respondent shall indemnify the 1st respondent in payment of compensation amount.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative and Issue No.3 Partly in the Affirmative.
In view of my findings on issues No.1 to 3, I pass the following:
ORDER The petition is allowed in part with cost.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.15,17,613/-(Rupees Fifteen lakhs seventeen thousand six hundred and thirteen only) with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 - 50%
 Petitioner No.2 - 15%
 Petitioner No.3 - 15%
 Petitioner No.4 - 20%
 After deposit of award amount, 40% of the amount apportioned in favour of Petitioner No.1 is ordered to deposit in her in any Nationalized Bank for a period of 3 years with liberty to draw the periodical interest and remaining amount is order to be released to Petitioners No.1 through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Entire compensation amount apportioned in favour of Petitioners No.2 to 4 is order to be released to them through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
